{"path":"snake_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete single-file Snake game (HTML + CSS + JS, no external dependencies) with the exact filename snake_zai-glm-5.3-flash_01.html. Requirements:

CORE SETUP
- One HTML file: doctype, <style> block, markup, <script> block. No external files/CDNs.
- Dark modern theme (dark background, neon green/orange accents), centered layout, Google-font-free (system fonts).
- Canvas rendering, 30x30 grid, cell size 20px → 600x600 canvas (scale down via CSS max-width for small screens).

GAME RULES
- Classic Snake on 30x30 grid. Snakes move continuously one cell per tick in one of 4 directions; grows by 1 segment when eating food; dies when hitting a wall (grid border), its own body, or the other snake's body.
- ONE shared food item, red apple, placed at random on a free cell (not on either snake).
- Tick interval: starts 110ms, speeds up slightly as total food eaten grows (min 65ms). Loop = requestAnimationFrame + time accumulator.
- Head-to-head: if both heads enter the same cell in one tick → both die → draw. If a head moves into the other head's old cell while the other moves into its (swap) → both die → draw.
- When any snake dies → game over screen; winner = surviving snake; if both died same tick → "Draw".

MODES (start menu)
1. Human vs Human — P1 green uses W/A/S/D, P2 orange uses Arrow keys.
2. CPU vs Human — P1 is CPU (green), human P2 uses Arrow keys.
3. CPU vs CPU — both CPU (green vs orange, spectator mode).
Menu shows title, three buttons (mouse clickable) and keyboard shortcuts 1/2/3. Also Enter starts the highlighted/last mode.

CPU AI
- Each tick CPU picks direction: candidates = 4 directions minus the reverse of current direction (no 180° turns).
- Filter to safe candidates: next cell inside grid and not occupied by any snake body segment (including its own tail; simple approximation: treat tail cell as occupied too — keep it simple).
- Among safe candidates prefer minimal Manhattan distance to food; tie-break randomly. If no safe candidate, keep current direction (will die).
- Slight imperfection is fine and desired (games should end).

INPUT
- Keyboard listener with preventDefault on arrows/space to avoid page scroll.
- Direction input per human snake goes into a small queue (max 2), so quick double-turns work; a queued direction is rejected if it's the reverse of, or equal to, the last applied/queued direction.
- P or Space toggles pause during play (show "PAUSED" overlay).
- Game over: R or Enter → restart same mode immediately; M or Escape → back to start menu.

UI SCREENS
- HUD bar above canvas during play: "Player 1" green score, "Player 2" orange score, current mode label, speed indicator optional.
- Start menu overlay (over the canvas): title "SNAKE", subtitle, 3 mode buttons with their controls described, footer hint "Press 1 / 2 / 3 to start".
- Game over overlay: big "GAME OVER", winner text (Player 1 wins / Player 2 wins / Draw), final scores of both, hints "R — Restart · M — Menu".
- Pause overlay.

RENDERING DETAILS
- Subtle checkerboard background on canvas; grid border stroke.
- Food: red circle with small green leaf/highlight.
- Snakes: rounded rectangles per segment; head slightly brighter with two small eye dots oriented by direction; body slightly fading toward tail.
- Dead snake flash or grey-out on last frame before overlay (optional).

CODE QUALITY
- Clean vanilla JS, const/let, no frameworks. Organize into: constants, state, Snake logic, AI, input, game loop, rendering, UI/screen management. Comments in English.
- Must run by double-clicking the file in a browser, no console errors.
Write the complete, working implementation."}
